title: Zeroizing CEK throughout decrypt path
description: The CEK is wrapped in Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> from the moment it is returned by find_and_decrypt_cek() and try_decrypt_kari(), ensuring it is scrubbed on drop at the end of decrypt(). This is the correct approach. A future contributor might suggest removing Zeroizing because 'the CEK is just bytes' — this would be wrong: the CEK is the key that protects message confidentiality and must be cleared.
close_reason: Confirmed: CEK is wrapped in Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> via find_and_decrypt_cek (return type on line 100). KTRI path wraps via Zeroizing::new() at line 118; KARI path wraps via Zeroizing::new(cek) at line 249. Good defensive practice.
